failure_modes: If a time-conditioned regional attention edit (C008-C011) were applied, the sign-reversing landmark contrasts could be tracked in the wrong direction at nodes where the curve reverses, displacing surrounding coordinates without an affinity benefit.

If a narrower or broader teacher-neighborhood count (C005-C007) were applied without dispersion evidence, mode coverage could shrink or mix competing directions, degrading the endpoint pointcloud reward.

If a distance-curvature edit (C001-C003) were applied without observed spatial-scale support, the endpoint-VJP force could be over- or under-scaled, moving coordinates unnecessarily while leaving final predicted affinity unchanged or worse.
rationale: Analyst's temporal evidence (F003-F005) shows the inspected landmark contrast curves are only validated as observed-node linear interpolations, with polynomial fits rejected, extrapolation disallowed, sign reversals and strong sign conflicts, and small mixed-sign whole-window z. H001's time-conditioned regional attention rule is therefore not yet defensible: the registered temporal_region/temporal_teacher choices (C008-C011) would change regional attention or blend a time-conditioned teacher, but the evidence does not establish that the time-conditioned rule reproduces the observed sign changes or beats a static rule on independent-batch agreement, and no decoded terminal affinity labels exist to show an affinity-first advantage. H002 is only weakly supported, so no landmark-priority edit is justified. The offered distance-curvature choices (C001-C003) and neighbor-count choices (C005-C007) are not tied to any read spatial-scale or dispersion evidence, and C004 is a region index with no supporting regional read. Since the objective is affinity-primary and no registered edit has a defensible expected advantage over the incumbent D2_without_trajectory_static, retaining the incumbent is the correct bounded action.
